terms.comment: Greek ἀμάρακος. Lewis & Short and Morgan–Owens: Origanum majorana. Lewis & Short gives it both genders, and a neuter amāracum; Morgan–Owens gives it as masculine. Pliny says that amāracum is what the Sicilians call the herb that Egypt and Syria call sampsūchum (NH 21.61). Morgan–Owens gives the medieval majorana beside it.
Greek σάμψυχον; also masculine sampsūchus (Celsus) and sampsūcum (Columella; Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: cinge tempora flōribus suāve olentis amāracī
phrases.english: bind your temples with the flowers of sweet-smelling marjoram

phrases.latin: ubi mollis amāracus illum flōribus et dulcī adspīrāns complectitur umbrā
phrases.english: where soft marjoram enfolds him in its flowers and sweet-breathing shade
